properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Changeable here: per-call option; verify:true restores sender+hash re-validation at the cost of failing on exotic tx types. Not an authentication gate — public chain data from an already-trusted RPC endpoint; the check is defense-in-depth against a lying/misbehaving node.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Ethereum's consensus signature scheme — observable here, replaceable only by an Ethereum protocol migration, not by this library. Deadline risk (forged signatures), not harvest-now-decrypt-later.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: After site-level judgment the object describes the 6 genuine hardcoded secp256k1 test-account private keys (published Anvil/Hardhat fixtures — real key material, no production secrecy); the 11 ERC20 token-address sites were rejected as false matches. Fixture hygiene note for a wallet library: test keys are fine as long as they stay the published Anvil-style accounts.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Object now describes the 9 confirmed keystore-fixture IV sites only; production encrypt generates a fresh random IV per keystore via the injected RNG (keystore.ts:610), so the literal IVs are deterministic test vectors, not a production reuse hazard. EIP-2335 mandates the IV be stored in cipherparams — a per-keystore random IV with no counter is the correct construction here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: EIP-2335 fixes the cipher to aes-128-ctr — not changeable without leaving the keystore format; integrity rests on the checksum MAC, not the mode.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: c=2000 at keystore.ts:1047 is the legacy presale format being READ for compatibility, not a new-encryption choice — the library must keep deriving those keys to decrypt old wallets.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Parameter set fixed by EIP-2335 (aes-128-ctr); cannot be strengthened without breaking keystore interop. Changeable only by the EIP, not this library.
